title: The Refund Ledger
text: Treasury lawyers walk you through how to repay importers after the Supreme Court said the emergency tariffs were not allowed. The ledger has many pages and no victories.

options.label: Sit through every page
options.result: Refund process drafted. You asked twice whether "refund" could be called "a bonus." It could not.

ignore.text: Importers filed suit. The ledger is now an exhibit, still unread.

inspiredBy: The Supreme Court struck down the IEEPA tariffs in February 2026, leaving open the question of refunds.

title: Signature Forensics
text: A specialist presents slides on whether a predecessor's pardons were signed by a machine. Slide 41 compares loops on the letter T.

options.label: Examine the loops
options.result: Findings inconclusive. Legal experts add that the machine was never the issue. You ask for a bigger pen.

ignore.text: The review stalled. The machine, reached for comment, said nothing.

inspiredBy: In June 2025 the president ordered a probe into a predecessor's alleged autopen use and the validity of his pardons.

title: Congressional Review Act Primer
text: A counsel explains how Congress can cancel old regulations with a simple majority and a tight deadline. There is a flowchart. There is a second flowchart.

options.label: Follow the flowcharts
options.result: Several rules were erased legally. The ceremony for this was a memo.

ignore.text: The deadline lapsed. The old rules live on, unbothered.

inspiredBy: In 2025 Republicans used the Congressional Review Act to overturn rules, including California vehicle waivers.

title: Byrd Bath
text: The Senate parliamentarian reviews your giant bill line by line. Several favorite provisions are ruled extraneous. No one will say "big" or "beautiful."

options.label: Listen to the rulings
options.result: Eleven provisions struck. The bill survives, slightly shorter and somewhat less beautiful.

ignore.text: Unreviewed, the bill was ruled out of order from start to finish.

inspiredBy: The Senate parliamentarian struck provisions from the 2025 tax and spending bill under the Byrd rule.

title: Injunction Reading Hour
text: A deputy summarizes the ruling that halted your order on mail voting. The word "exceeded" appears nineteen times.

options.label: Hear the whole ruling
options.result: Lawyers will appeal. The deputy now keeps a tally of "exceeded" for the next hearing.

ignore.text: The order stayed blocked. Nobody told the ballot printers.

inspiredBy: In June 2026 a federal judge blocked major parts of the president's executive order restricting voting by mail.

title: Partial Shutdown Status
text: The budget office briefs you on one department that has closed while the rest stays open. A flowchart shows which lights are on.

options.label: Review the map
options.result: Negotiators have been assigned. The flowchart is mostly red. You request more gold.

ignore.text: The department stayed closed. Its out-of-office message is now an official statement.

inspiredBy: A partial Homeland Security shutdown was under debate around the February 2026 State of the Union.

title: Emergency Docket Overview
text: The Solicitor General's office summarizes forty-one pending emergency applications. Each has a different acronym and a different deadline.

options.label: Sit for the full overview
options.result: Applications prioritized. You tried to name the docket after yourself and were told it has a name.

ignore.text: Three deadlines passed. A clerk filed one on a napkin.

inspiredBy: The administration filed a wave of emergency applications at the Supreme Court throughout 2025.

title: Fourth of July Signing
text: The giant spending bill reaches your desk on the holiday. The Speaker offers a ceremonial gavel and a flyover is on standby. Reading time is not scheduled.

options.label: Sign quietly, read it later
options.result: Signed with no jets. The gavel sits in a drawer, untouched, as intended.

options.label: Full ceremony with flyover
options.result: Bombers, a gavel and a speech about promises kept. Several clauses still unread by anyone.

ignore.text: The deadline slipped. The flyover circled for an hour, then went home.

inspiredBy: The president signed the One Big Beautiful Bill Act at a July 4, 2025 White House ceremony with a flyover.

title: Clemency Batch
text: A list of thirty names awaits your approval, some with friends in high places. The pardon office has written "vetted" above the list in pencil.

options.label: Run each case through review
options.result: Twenty-two names remain. The pencil note is now ink.

options.label: Announce them all by post
options.result: Posted with no names attached. The internet is now reading the rest as a mystery novel.

ignore.text: The list sat in a tray. Several would-be pardonees moved on to other hobbies.

inspiredBy: Large batches of pardons and commutations were announced in 2025 and again in September 2026.

title: Oval Office Signing
text: Sixteen executive orders are laid out for the cameras. A staffer notes you have only skimmed the first one. A reporter holds up a clipboard.

options.label: Read the orders first
options.result: You found a typo on page three. Counsel is now thrilled with you, which is its own problem.

options.label: Hold each one up for the cameras
options.result: The signing took an hour. Three orders were upside down. All were signed with bigger flourishes.

ignore.text: The pens dried out. The orders were signed by next Tuesday.

inspiredBy: The president signed dozens of executive orders in televised Oval Office sessions in 2025.

title: Nuke The Filibuster
text: You can post a demand that the Senate end the filibuster, or you can quietly count votes. The Senate has ninety-nine opinions on this.

options.label: Count the votes
options.result: There are not enough votes. This is shared with you gently, with a binder.

options.label: Post it in capital letters
options.result: The post was liked widely. The Senate leader said the rule will remain, then adjourned for lunch.

ignore.text: The shutdown dragged on. The filibuster remained smug.

inspiredBy: In late 2025 the president urged Senate Republicans to end the filibuster during the longest government shutdown.

title: The Map Wars
text: A mid-decade redistricting fight escalates. Your allies offer a new map that adds seats, and the other party is drawing a mirror map in reply.

options.label: Press for fair-map talks
options.result: Talks held. Both sides agreed the map was unfair, but only about the other one.

options.label: Demand more seats everywhere
options.result: States redraw. Constituents can no longer find their own districts, or the maps.

ignore.text: Two maps went to the courts. Judges are now holding them upside down.

inspiredBy: Mid-decade redistricting battles in Texas and California escalated in the second half of 2025.

title: Plan B For Tariffs
text: With the emergency tariffs struck down, an adviser offers a narrower, lawful route. The alternative statute is boring and has footnotes.

options.label: Use the narrow statute
options.result: The new tariffs are legal and small. You call them "stronger," and nobody knows in what sense.

options.label: Reimpose them under a new name
options.result: The tariffs return in a gold-trimmed disguise. Lawyers have already printed the next complaint.

ignore.text: No plan was chosen. Importers adopted a wait-and-see approach that cost billions.

inspiredBy: After the February 2026 Supreme Court ruling, the president promised stronger alternatives to the struck-down tariffs.

title: A Small Veto
text: A water project bill passed with support from both parties. A member of Congress you dislike sponsored it. The pen is right there.

options.label: Sign the bill
options.result: Water will flow. The sponsor sent a polite thank-you card you refused to open.

options.label: Veto it out of spite
options.result: Vetoed. Congress is discussing an override. The water is still waiting for its permit.

ignore.text: The bill became law without your signature. It is somehow still your fault.

inspiredBy: In December 2025 the president vetoed a Colorado water project bill and another measure favored by sponsors in both parties.

title: A Judge Says No
text: A federal judge has blocked a plan to cut staff across agencies. Your lawyers recommend an appeal. Your thumbs recommend a post.

options.label: Appeal through the courts
options.result: The appeal is filed. The judge reads it on a weekend and says "noted."

options.label: Denounce the judge online
options.result: The post was read by many. The Chief Justice issued a mild statement about judges that was read by few.

ignore.text: The order stayed in place. Staffers held a quiet party in the break room.

inspiredBy: In 2025 federal judges repeatedly blocked mass federal layoffs, and the president criticized judges publicly.

title: Four More Years, Again
text: A merchandise vendor presents a hat for 2028. Constitutional lawyers cite a certain amendment. The vendor says the hats are already sewn.

options.label: Decline the hats
options.result: The hats were donated to a golf pro shop. The amendment breathes a sigh of relief.

options.label: Order a thousand hats
options.result: The hats sold out. Scholars have published four papers titled "It Says Two."

ignore.text: The vendor made his own call. The hats are now collector items and a constitutional question.

inspiredBy: In 2025 the president and allies floated a third term despite the 22nd Amendment, and "Trump 2028" hats appeared.

title: Rename The Department
text: An order would rename the Department of Defense to "Department of War." Congress has not been consulted. A new sign is already in the shop.

options.label: Send it to Congress
options.result: A committee will study the sign. The sign is in a hallway, wrapped in plastic.

options.label: Sign the order, hang the sign
options.result: The sign is up. The statute still says "Defense," and so does the stationery.

ignore.text: The sign was hung without an order. The building is confused about itself.

inspiredBy: In September 2025 the president signed an order allowing "Department of War" as a secondary name for the Defense Department.

title: State Of The Union Draft
text: The draft speech runs ninety minutes. Your speechwriter suggests cuts. Your own notes suggest sixty more minutes of applause lines.

options.label: Cut it to an hour
options.result: A concise speech. The Chamber stays awake, and you spend an unsettling thirty minutes with no clapping.

options.label: Add the extra hour
options.result: A record is set. Several members have left the chamber for snacks and one for retirement.

ignore.text: No draft was approved. The Speaker began improvising a welcome.

inspiredBy: The February 2026 State of the Union lasted about 108 minutes, the longest on record.

title: Name The Savings Accounts
text: The new child savings accounts need a name on the forms. Treasury suggests "Child Savings Accounts." A staffer slides over a draft that says something else.

options.label: Keep the plain name
options.result: Forms printed. Parents understand them. You feel mildly unaccompanied.

options.label: Use your own name on them
options.result: The accounts carry your name. Budget analysts were more excited by the ones that do not.

ignore.text: The forms were printed with a blank. Parents filled in their own names, loudly.

inspiredBy: The 2025 tax and spending law created "Trump Accounts" savings accounts for children.

title: Reaction To The Ruling
text: Reporters want your response to the Supreme Court's ruling against your tariffs. Two of your own appointees voted against you. A microphone is already at your chin.

options.label: Say you will comply and appeal
options.result: A calm statement about "reviewing options." The press wrote it up as "strange but calm."

options.label: Call the Court a disgrace
options.result: Called a disgrace on live TV. Two justices have declined to comment, loudly.

ignore.text: No comment was given. Commentators wrote it for you.

inspiredBy: After the February 2026 tariff ruling the president called the decision "a disgrace."

title: Interview On 2028
text: A reporter asks about a third term. Your lawyer winces from off camera. The 22nd Amendment is, for once, trending.

options.label: Say you will honor the Constitution
options.result: Clear and brief. Aides exchange looks as the segment ends.

options.label: Smile and say "we'll see"
options.result: The clip ran all week. Constitutional scholars are now doing television, in shifts.

ignore.text: No answer was given. A hat vendor filled the gap.

inspiredBy: The president repeatedly teased the idea of a third term in 2025 despite the constitutional limit.

title: Signature Question
text: A reporter asks whether you sign everything by hand. The machine in the corner has not been used, but a staffer glances at it nervously.

options.label: Answer plainly
options.result: You explained the process. The machine remained a mere table decoration.

options.label: Hold up an oversized signature
options.result: The loops were huge, the ink was wet, and the White House counsel sighed.

ignore.text: The reporter wrote a long piece on signatures. It was not about yours.

inspiredBy: In 2025 the president attacked a predecessor's autopen pardons while also being asked about his own signing habits.

title: Joint Session Interview
text: Before an address to Congress, a reporter asks what you will say. Your speechwriter is shaking his head behind a pillar.

options.label: Keep the answer short
options.result: You gave the headlines. The surprise remained intact, for about a day.

options.label: Preview the whole speech
options.result: Forty minutes of preview. The actual address was now a rerun.

ignore.text: The reporter filled the gap with speculation. The address still ran long.

inspiredBy: The president addressed a joint session of Congress in March 2025 and again in February 2026.

title: The Gavel Question
text: A reporter asks about the ceremonial gavel and pen you collect at every signing. The collection now fills a vitrine, then a shelf, then a hallway.

options.label: Note they go to the archive
options.result: The archive is thrilled. It asked for the pens' receipts.

options.label: Say you have the best collection
options.result: Pens were ranked on live television. The Smithsonian has asked for a quiet word.

ignore.text: The question hung in the air. A pen rolled away.

inspiredBy: Signing ceremonies in 2025 featured pens, gavels and prop souvenirs handed to the president.

title: The Speaker Calls
text: The Speaker says the House is one vote short on your bill. Two holdouts want something in writing, and one wants a golf outing.

options.label: Offer small, honest concessions
options.result: Both holdouts relented. One kept the golf outing, the other got a tweaked paragraph.

options.label: Promise whatever they ask
options.result: Passed by 218 to 214. You promised a statue, a highway and a sandwich. All three are on the books.

ignore.text: The vote failed by one. The Speaker rehearsed a very long sigh.

inspiredBy: The One Big Beautiful Bill Act passed the House 218 to 214 in July 2025 after intense whip efforts.

title: Majority Leader On Nominees
text: The Senate leader says rules can be changed to confirm nominees in bundles, but it will cost you minority goodwill. The goodwill, he notes, is mostly theoretical.

options.label: Keep the rules as they are
options.result: The nominees wait their turn, which they find offensive and you find polite.

options.label: Change the rules to confirm them
options.result: Dozens confirmed in one vote. The minority called it a power grab, and then asked for a favor.

ignore.text: Nominees waited. Acting officials acted, and acted, and acted.

inspiredBy: In October 2025 Senate Republicans changed rules to allow en bloc confirmation of many nominees.

title: Solicitor General's Line
text: The Solicitor General says the appeals may go better if you stop posting about the judges. The line is silent as you consider this.

options.label: Let the lawyers talk
options.result: The brief was filed on time, and nobody mentioned any judge by nickname.

options.label: Post about the judges anyway
options.result: The posts were quoted verbatim in the other side's brief, in a font larger than yours.

ignore.text: The line went dead. The brief went in with two typos and a joke.

inspiredBy: Government lawyers filed a wave of emergency appeals in 2025 while the president criticized judges publicly.

title: The Pardon Czar
text: Your pardon czar has found a new batch of petitions. The list includes political allies, public figures and a man who sold a lot of fish.

options.label: Send them through the regular office
options.result: Slower. Most remained unpardoned, but the fish merchant is mid-review.

options.label: Say "pardon everyone"
options.result: A sweeping order. The czar made a spreadsheet. The spreadsheet made a face.

ignore.text: The petitions piled up. A few filed pardons for the pile itself.

inspiredBy: The White House pardon czar publicized batches of clemency grants in 2025 and September 2026.

title: State Senate Leader On The Map
text: A state senate leader says his chamber lacks the votes for a new congressional map. Several members have mixed feelings about being told what to do.

options.label: Accept the vote count
options.result: The map stays as it was. State senators sent a modest fruit basket.

options.label: Threaten primaries for "no" votes
options.result: The threat went public. The map failed anyway, and now there are primaries.

ignore.text: The vote happened without you. It was not close.

inspiredBy: In December 2025 the Indiana state senate rejected a mid-decade congressional map the White House had pushed.

title: Jury Duty
text: A jury summons has arrived at the White House, addressed to you. The clerk says everyone gets one eventually.

options.label: Request the standard deferral
options.result: Deferral granted by form letter. It began "Dear Resident," which stung.

options.label: Show up and ask to be foreman
options.result: You arrived with a motorcade and a verdict. The judge excused the entire panel.

ignore.text: A second summons arrived, in red ink. Then a third, addressed to "Occupant."

inspiredBy: Presidents and former presidents have periodically been summoned for jury duty.

title: Discovery Begins
text: A judge says your ten-billion-dollar suit against a foreign broadcaster may go ahead. Counsel notes this means they get to ask you questions too.

options.label: Settle for an apology
options.result: They apologized in a short, accented statement. No money changed hands. You framed the statement anyway.

options.label: Declare a huge victory and press on
options.result: You call it a huge victory. The broadcaster's lawyers have sent 300 questions and a date for your deposition.

ignore.text: The suit moved forward on its own. A deposition has been scheduled around your golf.

inspiredBy: November 2026: a judge ruled Trump's $10 billion defamation suit against the BBC could proceed. Trump called it a huge victory.
